markdown.golden:
# Working with PDF Fixtures

Test fixtures are small PDF files with known content. Each one is generated by a script, so its text, fonts and positions are documented and can be checked by tests without looking at the pages.

## Why fixtures matter

Real documents are messy and rarely redistributable. The project site at [example.org](https://example.org/fixtures) explains how the corpus is regenerated and verified.

### What a good fixture has

- Known text in a known place
- A documented reason to exist
- A size of a few kilobytes

![Page 1, image 1](images/p1-1.png)

## Two columns

The left column is read first, from top to bottom, before the reader moves to the right column.

The right column comes second. Its lines sit on the same baselines as the left column.
